headlines: Dragging is calm: sidebar rows stay put while a thin line shows where the one you hold will land, and project tabs glide aside smoothly.
Calmer sidebar and tabs: every project folder is one quiet colour again, and sections, projects and chats are easier to tell apart.
new: After a restart (an update, quitting, a crash) every project reopens as it was, and a chat that was cut off mid-way is marked "Interrupted by restart" with one Continue button. Continue tells it IDX restarted and to check the transcript and the working tree before carrying on; it is sent once. In a terminal chat the note is typed into the CLI after it resumes (Antigravity is only resumed, never typed into).

Settings ▸ General ▸ "Auto-continue interrupted work after restart" (off), with an On / Off choice per project: chats that were working carry on by themselves. A chat waiting for your approval or answer is never continued for you, and a Bypass or Auto chat only when its project is set to On.
improved: Sidebar drag (projects and chats): no row slides any more. The dragged row is lifted a little and one thin line marks the drop place; the order changes the moment you let go. Queued messages and browser tabs keep their slide.

Project tabs: the other tabs glide aside quickly while you drag, nothing moves when you pick a tab up, a drop settles without a snap, and Esc (or letting go outside the strip) glides the tab back. Dragging a tab out of the window still opens it in a new window.

Project folders no longer get a different colour each. Every folder icon is one calm colour; if you want a project to stand out, pick a colour for it in its menu (Project colour…), and Default puts it back. Colours you picked before are kept.

The sidebar has clearer layers without extra colour: section headers are small capitals, project names are bold, chats hang from a thin line under their project, and sections are divided by a hairline.

The chat or project you are on, and the project tab in front, are a raised surface that is easy to spot in both themes; hovering a tab highlights the whole tab, close button included, and New chat is set apart from the tabs.
Small colour fixes: hover in the dark sidebar is visible, status shapes in the light theme are a little stronger, and some grey text is easier to read.
fixed: A new Claude chat that opens in the terminal no longer starts anything until you press Start (or Enter): opening it creates no chat in the list and no Claude process, like a new chat in the chat view. Leave it and nothing is left behind.

headlines: The sidebar now lists only the projects you have open, in the same order as the tabs, and closing a project is safer and easy to undo. Dragging to reorder is live.
Chats in the terminal now get your attention: a notification, Dock badge and window count when a chat finishes or needs you.
new: Settings ▸ General ▸ "Notify when a chat finishes or needs me" (on) and "Play a sound with notifications" (off). A notification names the chat, appears only for a chat you are not looking at (another chat or project in front, or IDX in the background), and macOS Do Not Disturb silences it. A chat that needs you also bounces the Dock once; a finished reply only badges.

A finished reply stays marked (a check in the chat list and on the project tab) until you have looked at that chat; the Dock badge and the window title count chats that need you or finished unread, for example "(2) alpha". In a terminal scrolled up, a chip says "Claude is waiting for you" and the edge pulses once when the chat starts waiting.
Open project… (the + beside the tabs, ⌘K, or the sidebar) lists your recent projects first. Opening one adds it as a tab and a sidebar entry and brings it to the front.
improved: Terminal chats react to Claude Code sooner and more reliably: a permission dialog or question counts as soon as Claude Code asks (it used to wait for a later notification), and a prompt you answer by typing goes back to Working at once.

The sidebar shows only the projects you have open (the same ones, in the same order, as the project tabs). Closing a project removes it from the sidebar; its chats keep running and nothing is deleted. Other projects open from All projects, ⌘K or Open project…. A project that is closed but still working is listed under Running in closed projects, and a chat that needs you stays in Needs you (a click reopens the project).
Projects you had in the sidebar but not as tabs stay open this once, with a note, so nothing disappears; close the ones you are not using.

Closing a project: the close button is at the end of the tab with its own space, away from the icon you drag, and shows on hover or for the tab in front. A project with a working or waiting chat asks once before closing (Keep open is the default); otherwise it closes at once and a notice, kept for 8 seconds, has Undo (the project comes back in its place). Close project in the menus is its own group at the end.

Dragging to reorder is live: the other tabs, projects, chats, queued messages and browser tabs slide out of the way while you drag, the landing spot shows as a gap, a long list scrolls when you hold near its edge, and the dropped item settles into place. With reduced motion they jump instead of sliding.
fixed: A terminal chat that needed you was never announced while IDX was in front, even when another chat was showing. A finished reply and a prompt right after it no longer swallow each other, and the notification no longer plays a sound unless you turn that on.

Switching windows no longer marks a waiting terminal chat as seen (the terminal's focus reports counted as typing), and pressing Esc to interrupt Claude no longer leaves the chat showing Working forever.

Several projects could end up with the same colour (four of five were salmon). A new project now gets the colour least used by your other projects, and keeps it; the colours you picked yourself are never changed.
The red, amber and pink project colours looked like errors or warnings. Project colours now run from olive to pink, none of them in the red or amber range that means danger.

headlines: Approvals and Quit are safer: a new approval can no longer be answered by a key you typed before it appeared, and Quit warns about chats waiting on you.
The sidebar is easier to scan: projects, chats and states each look different, and projects keep the order you drag them into, in the sidebar and the tabs alike.
improved: Sidebar: a project row has its icon in its own colour and a bold name; its chats sit under it, lighter, each starting with its state. States differ by shape, not only colour: a spinner while working, a diamond when it needs you, a check when finished, a cross on an error, an empty ring when stopped.

The permission mode shows once, as a small badge, only where it differs: on a chat that runs in another mode than its project, or on a project that differs from new chats. Red only for Bypass. It no longer repeats "Mode: Bypass" under every chat.

Chat steps are easier to read: a command step is titled by what it does ("Encode 720p proxies"), not by the shell script; the command itself sits behind a Command button with Copy and is never shown twice. A failed step shows its one-line reason under the title, a call that never ran says what went wrong and that Claude retried, and a command started in the background says so instead of "exit 0".

A chat no longer shows its own title again as its preview, every time in the sidebar is the time since the last activity (hover for the date), every section header looks the same, and "New chat" appears once (other projects have a + on hover).

One project order for the sidebar and the project tabs: drag a project in either (or use Move up / down / to top) and the other follows; it is kept after a restart. Other projects ▸ ⋯ ▸ Sort: Recent or Manual. A grip appears on hover to show a project can be dragged.

Background work: jobs Claude leaves running (an upload, an encode, a dev server) now show at the foot of the chat with their name, how long they have run, their last reported line (and a bar when it reports a percentage), Stop and Open output. Before, they were only a small Running badge in the header, and the status line said just "Working".
Settings ▸ General ▸ Project tabs: turn the tabs at the top off to use the sidebar alone.
Ages in lists switch from days to months and years after 30 days (a year-old chat no longer reads "366d").

The status line at the foot of a working chat names the step in words: when Claude described a command ("Encoding proxies") that sentence shows with the time, instead of the raw shell line, and it says how many jobs run in the background behind it.
A usage-limit reset more than a week away now names its date, so "Mon" on a Monday is no longer ambiguous.

Project colours are brighter and clearly different from each other in both themes, so a tab icon never looks grey or "special" for no reason. Pick one in the project menu (Project colour, or Automatic); it shows on the tab, Home, the sidebar and ⌘K. Hover the icon: it says "Project colour" so it is never mistaken for a status.
The chip at the top of a chat that said "Tasks · 1" now says what it counts ("Running · 2", or "Finished · 1"), explains itself on hover, and opens the list of jobs and sub-agents when clicked.

Files Claude sends you are easier to read and open: a picture is a readable thumbnail (up to 320 px wide, a tall one shows its top) with its name, size and pixel size; any other file is a card with its kind and size; a file that is gone says so calmly. They sit under the answer text that introduces them. Click opens the file in Details, ⌘-click opens your editor, right-click gives Reveal in Finder and Copy path.
fixed: Dragging a folder from Finder into the window now opens it as a project wherever you drop it: the project tabs, the top bar, Home, the chat or any empty space (it used to work only on the sidebar and the Projects list). The window shows one highlight while you drag, says "Opened <name>", a folder dropped on the message box still attaches and offers "Open as project", a file dropped outside the message box says where to drop it, and a missed drop can no longer replace the app with the dropped file. A folder dropped on the Dock icon or opened with Open With also opens as a project.

A permission or question card that arrives while you type in the message box no longer takes the keyboard: your next Space or Enter stays in the box instead of pressing Allow. Keys 1, 2 and 3 answer only when nothing else has focus, and not in the first moment after a card appears.

A failed check for updates (for example with no internet) is no longer a permanent message in the sidebar: it is a quiet note in Settings > About that you can dismiss, and the app keeps trying again in the background.

Quitting or restarting to update used to ignore a chat paused on an approval or a question, and gave up checking after a second and a half and quit anyway. It now lists every chat that is working or waiting for you, Cancel is the default, and if IDX cannot check it asks instead of quitting. An update never restarts the app by itself.
At most three notifications show at once, newest on top; a repeat of the same message replaces it, and the stack always stops above the message box so Send stays clickable in small windows.
Settings made in one window (Trust level, Bypass confirmations, per-project choices) are no longer overwritten by another open window. Windows now pick up each other's changes straight away.
Error notifications stay about 15 seconds, are announced to screen readers, and any notification waits while the pointer or keyboard focus is on it.
The tip over an answer’s Retry, Copy and Fork buttons no longer covers the answer text: it opens below the row.

headlines: A chat the Claude CLI could not open ("Session ID is already in use") no longer dead-ends: it opens, or you can start it over in one click.
fixed: Opening a chat in the terminal no longer fails with "Session ID ... is already in use" when an earlier terminal start left nothing but start-up lines behind. The chat gets a fresh conversation id and keeps its title and settings.

When the Claude CLI refuses a chat ("already in use" or "No conversation found"), the terminal shows one line with "Start this chat over". Earlier history is not carried over, because the CLI has none to carry. The same action is in the chat menu for a chat with nothing said in it.
A chat that exists but has no messages now says "This chat has no messages yet" instead of "Start a chat".

headlines: A question or approval on a stopped chat can now be answered: one click resumes the chat and sends your answer.
An old "Weekly limit reached" no longer lingers on the new-chat box.
fixed: The red "Weekly limit reached" no longer stays on the new-chat box after your account has answered again. Settings > Diagnostics and the chip tooltip say why a limit is shown.

Answering a question or approval in a chat that is not running no longer fails with "Session is not running". The card says "Session stopped", keeps your answer, and "Resume and send answer" restarts the chat and sends it as your next message with the question quoted.
Needs you shows a stopped chat's waiting request as "Stopped · question waiting", and its count now matches "waiting" under Quick chats.
Esc now closes the right-click menu in a terminal.

headlines: "Weekly limit reached" no longer shows when your account still works.
Files open one way everywhere: a click shows them in Details, ⌘-click opens your editor.
improved: Opening a file works the same in the chat, the terminal, the Files list and the diff: a click opens it in Details (at the line when there is one), ⌘-click opens it in your editor, right-click gives Open, Reveal in Finder and Copy path. Settings > General > Open files with swaps the two.
A picture or file Claude sends is one control that opens in Details. The extra Preview button and the pop-up picture window are gone, and a second click no longer closes it.
HTML pages and pictures in Details now fill the panel instead of sitting in a small box.
A file that was moved or deleted shows a calm note with Locate and Copy path instead of an error.
fixed: "Weekly limit reached" (and the red limit chip) showed up when your account was fine. It now shows only when Claude actually refuses a message, clears the moment a newer report says you are fine, a real answer arrives, or the reset time passes, and only for the account and model it is about.
Getting close to a limit is a calm note on the usage chip ("85% of this week's limit · resets Sun 3:30 PM"), never a stop.
Settings > Diagnostics shows the last limit report Claude sent for each account, so any doubt can be settled at a glance.
Follow agent in Details is no longer switched on by a stray F key (it is now Option+F) and no longer stays on after a restart.
In shell mode the note "The agent reads the output with your next message" hides when the message box is too narrow for it, so it never sits on top of the account chip.

headlines: Type ! first in the message box to run a command on this Mac, like in the Claude Code CLI.
new: Shell mode: a ! first in the message box switches it to shell mode ("Shell · runs on this Mac in <folder>"). Enter runs the command in the project folder with the same setup as the Terminal tab; the output streams into the chat as a "You ran" row with its exit code and time, a Stop button, Copy, and the full text in Details. After a command runs the box goes back to a normal message; type ! again for the next one. Esc, or Backspace on an empty box, leaves shell mode; Ctrl+C on an empty box stops the running command. The agent reads the commands and their output with your next message. It never runs anything the agent suggested, and not while an approval is waiting. Settings ▸ General can turn it off.
improved: Ctrl+S in the message box stashes your draft (text, shell mode and attachments) and clears the box; on an empty box it brings the newest stash back, like the Claude Code CLI. A quiet line above the box shows what is stashed, with Bring back and Drop.
Ctrl+G opens your draft in the editor chosen in Settings and takes the text back each time you save the file; Done ends it. Option+P opens the model list.
Up and Ctrl+R in the message box also bring back the commands you ran with !, in shell mode.

headlines: The message box keeps more of the Claude Code habits: Up recalls your prompts from every chat of the project, and Shift+Tab changes the mode.
A long paste shows as a Pasted text chip in your message too, and the chat always says what it is doing right now.
improved: Chat > Previous Prompt and Next Prompt (Control-Command-Up and Down) walk your own prompts in a long chat; past the last one you land at the end of the chat.
Ctrl+R in the message box searches your earlier prompts, like the Claude Code CLI: type to filter, Up and Down to choose, Enter puts one in the box (it never sends), Esc keeps what you had.

Shift+Tab in the message box cycles the mode (Ask first, Accept edits, Plan only) like the Claude Code CLI. Esc twice or Ctrl+C clears what you typed, and Up brings it back; Ctrl+C on an empty box while a turn runs asks to stop.

Up in the message box recalls your earlier prompts from every chat of the project, not only this one, like the Claude Code CLI. A new chat has them too. One press steps one prompt (a two-line prompt takes one extra press to cross its lines).

A long paste is a "Pasted text · N lines" chip in the message box and in the sent message: open it in place, copy the full text, remove it with one click or Backspace. The agent still gets every line.
File chips in the message box show their size and type, and open in Finder. A long prompt read back from a terminal chat folds to its first lines with Show all.

One status line at the bottom of the chat says what is happening now: "Working · Bash npm test · 42s", "Waiting for 3 agents", "Sent · waiting for the model", or that a background task is still running. It is there only while something is happening.
While a sub-agent runs, its step shows as a chip right in the chat, so you see what it is doing without opening Details.
After 15 seconds without output it says when the last output was; after 90 seconds it says "No output for 1m 30s, still working" and shows Stop.
fixed: Sending a message while you are scrolled up in a long chat now takes you to the bottom, so your message and the answer are on screen.

headlines: Adding an account starts with six plain choices that say what each costs and where you sign in.
Details opens long output, changes, plans, files and pictures at full size, with search, previews, back / forward and an optional Follow agent.
new: Google accounts show their route: Gemini CLI or Antigravity. A Gemini Google sign-in says Route not confirmed until you note it has a Code Assist licence, because Gemini CLI stopped serving free, Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra accounts on 18 Jun 2026.

Add account: pick from six kinds (Claude subscription, Claude API key, Gemini API key, Gemini Google sign-in, Cloud or enterprise, Antigravity), with a comparison of what each can do and which sign-in opens your browser.
An account's information now lists what it can do and what it cannot.
Browser panel tabs can be reordered: drag a tab, or press the Move Tab Left and Move Tab Right keys. The order is remembered for each project.

Queued messages can be reordered: Move earlier and Move later, a drag handle, or Option with the up and down arrows on the handle. The agent reads them in your order, and nothing moves unless you move it.
Long code blocks in an answer fold to the first lines with Show all N lines. Copy still copies everything; Detail level Everything opens them.
Pictures a tool returns (Claude reading a PNG, a screenshot) show under the step and open full size in Details; they come back after a restart.
Gemini chats use the same chips and Details: a sub-agent step, the plan it wrote, changed files and its checklist. Only what Gemini sends is shown.
Long command output, edits, the plan and the to-do list open in Details: search a long log, show only errors, copy or save it, see a change or the plan at full size.

Files Claude writes, edits or sends can be previewed in Details: Markdown, images, SVG, PDF, HTML (scripts off), CSV as a table, JSON as a tree, notebooks, text and code, with Source and Changes tabs.
Details has Back and Forward (Option plus the arrow keys) and a Follow agent switch, off by default, that shows the running sub-agent without moving your focus.
A running sub-agent shows a short line about what it is doing. Settings > General > Sub-agent progress lines turns it off (it costs a little).
improved: Accounts made in older versions keep their folders and settings untouched. Two accounts that share a name are flagged with a Rename button.
Share my setup now also shares your plugins (read from your own folder, read-only) and your MCP servers with a Claude account. MCP servers that hold a sign-in are left out and named.
Pin an account as a project's default for new chats from the account menu. A pay-per-token account can never be pinned.

A chat can move to another account of the same tool from the account button in the message box. A short note first says what changes: billing, features, limits and where the history lives. It only ever happens when you choose it.

Share my setup for a Gemini account now copies your Gemini settings (without anything that could carry a sign-in) each time the account starts, so your MCP servers and preferences show up there. Instructions and extensions are still linked.
Previous Chat and Next Chat follow the order you see in the sidebar: pinned first, then recent, in the order you set. A chat that needs you is no longer jumped to first (use Next Needs You for that).
One wording for chats that wait on you: Needs you, in the sidebar, the Dock menu and the project browser.
fixed: The What's new card no longer shows on a first install, only after an update.

headlines: New chats start the way you left them: view, permission mode, model and effort.
A Details panel for sub-agents, many Terminal upgrades, and a What's new card after every update.
new: What's new: after an update a quiet card tells you what changed. Help > What's New and Settings > About list every version.
The update button now shows the top one or two changes before you restart.
New chats start in the permission mode, model and effort you last used in that project, separately for Claude and Gemini.
Settings > Trust & permissions: Start new chats in the mode I used last, with an off switch.
Same as last time: a new chat opens in Chat or Terminal, whichever you used last in that project.
Details panel beside the chat, with a chip for each sub-agent.
Terminal: find in scrollback, clickable file paths, a Scroll to bottom button, Clear Terminal, a right-click menu and Copy on select (off by default).
Terminal scrollback setting: 5,000, 20,000 or 50,000 lines, with the memory it uses.
Terminal text size has its own keys (Control-Command plus, minus and 0).
improved: Chats come back after a restart in the view you left them in, Chat or Terminal.
A chat in Bypass is always named in the sidebar and the mode button says where the mode came from.
A Claude chat started in the terminal now begins with your chosen model and effort.
Bypass used in one project is never carried into a project that has not confirmed it.
Release notes on GitHub now come from the same list as the in-app What's new.
When a plan limit is reached, a calm strip lets you switch account yourself and reminds you at reset. Stopped chats get a Resume button.
A message blocked by your own hook shows as one row with a count and the hook message to copy.
Sub-agent steps come back when you import or catch up a chat from the terminal.
Short messages no longer stretch wide, and repeated output lines fold into one.
Files and Diff lists, and long Settings lists, fold open and shut the same way everywhere.

headlines: Send now and Redirect while Claude works, plus a Detail level for how much each chat shows.
Antigravity joins Claude and Gemini, and every account has its own folder.
new: Chat width: Auto, Narrow, Medium, Wide or Full, one click from the chat header, kept per project and per window.
Stop chat frees a chat's memory and keeps it in your list. Stopped chats show as an outline.
Send now (Ctrl+Enter) and Redirect while Claude is working. You can also write while an approval or question waits.
Antigravity (agy) is a choice next to Claude and Gemini. It opens as a terminal you type into, with its own accounts.
Every account has its own folder, with Reveal in Finder and Copy path. Share my setup lets a new account use your instructions, skills, agents and commands by reference.
An information panel on every account, and a Connected accounts strip at the top of Settings > Accounts.
Detail level: Summary, Normal or Everything, in the chat menu, Settings and the command palette.
Copy from terminals: the whole scrollback, the last lines, the screen or your selection. Also Copy session as Markdown and Save as file.
Open links in IDX's browser, your default browser, or ask each time. IDX remembers your choice per site.
Tool server (MCP) questions show as a card you can answer. Settings > Connections shows each server's state with Reconnect and Turn off.
Thinking effort, Fast mode and Output style pickers, shown only where your model and account support them.
Plan usage in the message box: 5-hour and weekly limits and reset times.
Background tasks: Move to background, and the Needs you list says how many are running.
Sidebar sections: Needs you, This project and Other projects. Drag chats or use Move to top, up and down to set your own order.
improved: Clearer screens: each fact is shown once and each thing has one name. The status dots have a legend.
A step that fails opens by itself, and closed rows say what is inside. IDX remembers which ones you opened in each chat.
Typing in a terminal and the first words of a reply reach the screen sooner.
Sign in, Check and Diagnose on accounts now work and show what is happening.
fixed: The Browser panel's buttons no longer run off the edge in a narrow window.
The Thinking effort picker now appears for models that support it.

headlines: Rewind: go back to any of your prompts and restore the code, the conversation, or both.
Updates are clearer: Skip this version, and Check for updates always answers.
new: Rewind to here beside every prompt you sent. Also /rewind, the command palette, or Esc twice in an idle chat.
A small panel shows the files that would change before anything happens. Restoring only the conversation is the safe default.
Skip this version for an update you do not want yet.
improved: If a newer update comes out while one is already downloaded, IDX swaps to the newer one.
Check for updates always answers: checking, up to date (with the time), downloading with a percentage, or a plain reason with Retry.
The same update status shows in the sidebar footer, Settings > About and the app menu.
IDX no longer asks you to restart while your chats are working.
In a narrow window, choosing a Settings section closes the section list.

headlines: Esc on a running chat now asks first, so a slip never stops your work.
Pictures you attach or paste now load and enlarge reliably.
new: Esc on a running chat asks first. Enter stops it, Esc keeps it going. The setting Stop with a single Esc turns the question off.
A stopped chat shows a quiet Stopped by you line with Continue and Retry last prompt. The work done so far is kept.
improved: Several Thinking steps in a row fold into one line.
A tool header shows the first useful line of a script, with Show more for the rest.
A tool call that failed and was retried shows one quiet line.
The approaching-your-limit notice shows once, above the message field.
When a hook has a problem, the line names the hook and says it comes from your own Claude settings.
Tables scroll sideways instead of squashing their columns.
fixed: Attached and pasted images no longer show as blank boxes. IDX keeps its own copy of each picture. A picture that cannot load shows Retry and Remove.

headlines: Put up to three live chats of a project side by side.
A Needs you sheet gathers every waiting question across your columns.
new: Chat columns: open up to three live chats of one project side by side, with Open in new column in a chat's menu.
An approvals rail and a Needs you sheet gather every question waiting for you across the columns.
On wide windows the sidebar shows a short preview under each chat.
improved: The tab strip keeps its buttons on screen when a project has a long name.
Shortcut tips appear above the message box instead of covering it.
The Gemini approval card has clearer wording.
Open in is a submenu, and the sidebar tip card can be collapsed.
Panel tabs, chat header chips, the command palette and Settings rows fit better in small windows. Tooltips no longer linger.

headlines: Display size for big screens, with Auto for 4K.
Mac permissions in one place, with no surprise prompts.
new: Settings > Trust & permissions > Mac permissions lists what IDX can use, as Recommended, Optional and Never asked, each with its status.
A first-run permissions walk, and a banner if a permission is switched off later.
Automation guard (off by default): stops chats from driving other Mac apps through osascript.
Settings > Appearance > Display size: Auto, Compact, Default, Comfortable, Large or Extra large, with a per-window override.
improved: No text under 12 px at the default size. Chat and message text is a little larger.
Muted and secondary text is clearer in light and dark.
Section headings are firmer and there is more space above each of your prompts.
IDX is now private and proprietary software instead of Apache-2.0.

headlines: IDX can answer low-risk approvals for you while you are away.
Every reply ends with the model, tokens and time it took.
new: Smarter approvals: IDX judges how risky a request is and can answer low-risk ones for you. Questions that wait too long fall back to a safe default.
Diagnostics > Approvals lists every approval and what was decided.
Every reply ends with a footer: the model, the tokens used and how long it took.
A models-used-in-this-chat panel.
improved: Switching models shows one clear Switched to line instead of a pile of them.
Sandboxes are never cleaned up automatically. You can still pick a clean-up period in Settings.
Tidying up empty chats runs once to clear leftovers from earlier versions, then only if you turn it on.

headlines: One project per window, and a quick switcher: press Command-P to jump anywhere.
Archived chats now have a page you can find.
new: One project, one window: lock a window to its project, send a project to another window with Move to Window, and pull it back with Bring Here. A Window menu lists your windows.
Archived chats have their own page in the sidebar and can be restored in place. After you archive, a message tells you where it went.
Command-P jumps to any project or chat. Control-Tab cycles through them.
Redraw terminal repaints a terminal that looks garbled.
improved: The header shows the project name in its accent colour.
Chat titles are short and clean, and a name you set yourself always wins.
Started chats keep their own model. Empty chats left over from earlier versions are archived.
Shortcut tips adapt: after you click an action a few times, IDX shows its shortcut once, then stops.
fixed: Long names and narrow windows no longer overflow or overlap.

headlines: A new chat stays a draft until you send the first message.
Trust levels per project, and a shortcuts guide.
new: Trust levels per project, pre-trusting a folder, an always-allow list, a macOS permissions guide and a terminal hand-off mode.
A shortcuts guide, key hints next to actions and a once-a-day tip.
A new chat stays a draft until you send the first message.
Phone access is off by default. Turn it on per chat with Continue on phone.
improved: How many chats can run at once now follows your Mac's real memory, and idle chats stop on their own in Automatic mode.
Low-memory warnings only appear when memory is genuinely low.
The model shown on a chat is the model that actually answered.
fixed: Menus open next to the button you clicked, including the chat menu mid-chat.

headlines: Right-click the Dock icon to see chats waiting for you.
Idle chats free their memory, with nothing left running after you quit.
new: Dock menu: chats waiting for you, pinned and recent projects, and quick actions. Window titles are now meaningful.
improved: Sidebar chat names are meaningful, and screenshot names read properly.
Idle chats stop and free memory, and there are no leftover processes after you quit.
No dollar amounts are shown on Max plans.
fixed: /compact no longer shows raw text in the transcript, and hook noise is hidden.

headlines: Links and files open beside the chat.
Each reply shows which model answered it.
new: Gemini 4 Argon is built in, tagged Early.
Links in chat open beside the chat and can be copied. Files mentioned in a chat open there too.
Files Claude sends show as previews in the chat.
Each reply shows which model answered it, and a Switched to line appears when the model or account changes.
improved: Gemini thinking is readable, with proper formatting.
The Gemini chat header shows the model and the account.

headlines: Sandboxes are full projects you can keep, and Claude in a terminal is a first-class choice.
Reopening IDX brings back every window, tab and terminal.
new: New sandbox (Control-Command-N) opens an empty, git-ready project in its own tab. Keep moves it to a folder you pick, with all its chats. Discard sends it to the Archive.
An All chats page lists your chats from every project.
Start any chat in the Claude terminal with Option-Command-T, or flip a chat with the Chat | Terminal switch.
Add projects straight from a previous tool, read-only, in one step.
improved: A chat only asks for you when Claude really needs an answer. Terminal bells and idle prompts no longer set it off.
Fast, exact restore: every window on its display at its size, every tab and the shell scrollback. Only the chats in front start; the rest resume when you open them.
The place menu is one menu everywhere.

headlines: Checked against Gemini CLI 0.64.0.
improved: Everything IDX uses was checked against Gemini CLI 0.64.0: chats, model and mode lists, approvals, file edits and finished replies.
Settings > Diagnostics notes when your Gemini CLI is newer than the versions IDX was checked with.
fixed: A Gemini chat you continued in the terminal now reads back correctly after Gemini shortens a long conversation. Earlier turns could show up twice.

headlines: Command-W now closes what you are working in, like a browser.
Command-Shift-T brings back what you just closed.
new: Command-W closes whatever has focus: a Browser or Terminal tab, the Files or Diff panel, the terminal drawer, or the chat in front. Nothing is deleted, and Command-Shift-T brings it back.
Closing a terminal tab that is still running something asks first.
improved: A Claude chat that has finished replying shows as done, even if its reply ends with a question. Waiting means a real question, permission or plan approval.
New chat in this project, for a project open in another window, starts the chat in that window with your cursor in the message box.
Closing a pop-out window from the keyboard puts its chat back in the project window.

headlines: IDX opens about a second sooner.
Gemini models have clear names, and you can type a model it does not list yet.
new: Drag a folder onto the sidebar or Home to add a project. After adding a folder or starting a chat, your cursor is already in the message box.
Many project tabs: an N more menu lists the tabs that do not fit.
Type a Gemini model id the CLI does not list yet. After you use it once, it stays in the menu for that account.
improved: IDX no longer waits for your shell settings before showing the window. Chats and terminals still get your full setup.
Gemini model names are clear, with the most capable first.
In a new chat, the model and mode menus show the chosen agent's real choices before you send anything.
Once a chat has started, the account chip shows the account's name.
The browser start page has a single address bar.
fixed: A Gemini chat that finished replying shows as done, not waiting.
Archiving a project from its own window closes that window.

headlines: A chat you pop out into its own window now stays on that chat.
fixed: Moving or resizing a popped-out chat window, or relaunching, could switch it to the Home screen. It now keeps showing the chat and its message box.
This works the same for project chats, quick chats, and chats popped out of a project's own window.

headlines: Nothing gets cut off in a small window any more.
improved: Menus always fit inside the window, wrap long descriptions and never open under the window buttons.
Dialogs fit a short window and scroll inside.
Project tabs no longer overlap each other or the plus button. The strip scrolls and keeps your tab in view.
Usage bars line up across accounts, turn amber from 80% and red from 95%.
Custom endpoint choices are clear segmented buttons.
A list filtered to nothing says so. The sidebar fades out under Home and New chat when scrolled.
A chat continuing in the terminal shows a small terminal icon in the sidebar.
Settings opens full width. The Send button looks clearly off when there is nothing to send.
fixed: Report an Issue no longer includes log lines written by earlier versions.

headlines: Small fixes to account usage.
fixed: Settings > Diagnostics > Account usage: each account's name and plan are readable again, with the usage bars beside them.
The usage heads-up above the message box reads plainly, for example has used 90% of its weekly limit.
Usage percentages line up better.

headlines: Accounts with plan names, usage meters and custom endpoints.
The chat and the terminal stay in sync when you switch between them.
new: Rename any account. Each account shows its plan and email, for example Work - Max.
Usage meters for each Claude account (5-hour and weekly), and a calm heads-up at 80%.
Custom endpoint accounts for an AI gateway or local models such as Ollama and LiteLLM.
Continue a chat in the terminal and the chat waits, so the two never both write. What you do in the terminal appears in the chat, and Return to chat picks up from there.
If the terminal went in a different direction, the chat shows it as a branch.
improved: Menus and pop-ups never get cut off at the edge of the window.
The model picker is one simple list: Auto at the top, then each model with a short note.
The sidebar no longer jumps around when you click. Pinned projects stay where you put them.
Hundreds of projects and chats are fine: All projects and Show all chats open a fast, searchable list.
Opening a project always does the same thing: if it is open in a window, go there; otherwise open it as a tab.
fixed: A chat no longer fails to open when one of its saved context readings was incomplete.
Gemini: the first reply after returning from the terminal is no longer lost.

headlines: A Chrome-grade Browser panel, and accounts with their own sign-ins.
Tabs and terminal scrollback survive a restart.
new: A Browser panel with dev-server detection, device mode, zoom and pop-out.
Settings > Accounts: Claude, Gemini and Antigravity accounts, each with its own sign-in.
Settings > Diagnostics and Report an Issue, which builds a local bundle you can read first. Nothing is uploaded.
Project-first navigation: a Projects home and a project sidebar.
Tabs and terminal scrollback survive a relaunch, and nothing re-runs by itself.
improved: Chats and terminals pick up your full shell setup, including PATH.
Differential updates verify correctly.

headlines: See what Claude's sub-agents are doing, live.
IDX works more like the terminal: queued messages, plan approval, readable steps.
new: Sub-agents show as cards under the reply, live, with their own steps, tokens and a Stop button.
A Running tray lists background commands and sub-agents, each with Stop.
A context meter shows how full the conversation is. Compact now compacts it and leaves a marker.
Open and continue chats you started in a terminal. IDX warns you before both write to the same chat.
Phone access per chat: share a chat with the Claude app.
Environment variables per profile.
Gemini CLI runs in the chat view, for paid, API-key and company plans.
improved: A message you send while Claude works is queued and folded into the turn.
Chats start in your Claude Code default mode. Thinking summaries are shown.
Readable tool steps: commands with output, files read, edits with inline diffs, searches with match counts.
Proper plan approval, questions answered as choices, and Deny and tell Claude why.
Ask first now always asks before an edit, even when a plugin hook would have approved it.
Banners for retries and usage limits. Messages from your hooks show as small rows.
fixed: The chat no longer gets stuck on Working.
Claude transcripts are always saved, even when IDX was opened from inside another Claude Code session.

headlines: Closing a tab no longer archives it, and a restart brings everything back.
A new chat creates nothing until you send.
new: Archive is separate from closing, with Undo. Command-Shift-T reopens closed tabs, pop-outs and windows.
Restart brings back your half-typed message in every chat, your scroll position and everything that was open.
Each chat has its own message box.
A note appears when two chats work in the same folder.
improved: Command-N creates nothing until you send. Quick chats get readable folder names.
Faster and steadier: no jumping while replies stream, and one Claude process per chat.
A calm, consistent motion style, and clearer wording: chat, project, quick chat, Save as project.
Open in own window is visible on projects and quick chats.
fixed: The terminal tab name, diff colours, header alignment, and a waiting chat listed twice.

headlines: A calm new look with no purple.
Pop a chat, terminal, diff or file out into its own window.
new: Pop a chat, terminal, diff or file out into its own window (Option-Command-N) and dock it back (Option-Command-B). Pop-outs come back after a restart.
The model list shows before your first message.
improved: Calm new look: buttons are off-white in dark and graphite in light, the focus ring is quiet, and plan status is teal.
Code blocks, diffs and the terminal are light in light mode. Code blocks wrap.
Your data folder is private to you. A smaller app download.
A popped-out chat shows its title once, Command-K lists each chat once, and error messages are plain.

headlines: A new app icon, and a quick terminal drawer under the chat.
Quick chats move to their own list in the sidebar.
new: Quick terminal drawer under the chat: Control-backtick toggles it, Esc goes to the terminal, Command-L takes you back to the chat.
Open in lists your installed editors: Cursor, Finder, VS Code, Zed, Xcode.
Quick chats move to a Chats list in the sidebar. The top strip keeps your folders and pinned chats, with Pin and Unpin in the chat menus.
A signed and notarized install DMG.
improved: A new app icon: graphite and warm white, with a matching IDX Dev icon.

headlines: A Restart to update button in the top bar, and chats that survive sleep.
new: A Restart to update button appears in the top bar when an update is ready. It warns you if chats are still running.
Settings > Data & privacy with Remove all IDX data, and Help > Uninstall IDX.
A branded install window when you open the download.
improved: Your chats and the background service survive your Mac going to sleep.
Dev builds are fully IDX Dev, with an amber DEV icon, so they never get mixed up with the real app.

headlines: IDX finds Claude Code wherever it is installed.
new: Set the Claude Code path in Settings > General, and use Detect to find it for you.
Home shows whether Claude Code is installed and signed in, with a one-click Sign in.
improved: If Claude Code is missing, your message is never lost, and you get clear buttons to fix it.

headlines: Smart paste, drag-and-drop, slash commands and @ file mentions in the message box.
new: Message box: smart paste, drag-and-drop, / commands and @ file mentions.
A Help menu, and each window is titled after its chat.
Command-Q warns you if chats are still running.
improved: Dev builds are a separate IDX Dev app, so they never mix with the real one.
Check for Updates always gives an answer, and a notification appears when an update is ready.
Menus work with no window open, and relaunching from the Dock opens a window.

headlines: The first release: a signed, notarized IDX with auto-update.
new: The first signed and notarized release, with automatic updates.
